newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian police search for 13 children in outback.
newsitem.headline: Australian police search for 13 children in outback.

text.p: An Aboriginal woman and 13 children, including an infant, have gone missing in a remote area of Western Australia state, police said on Monday.
The group had set out to gather native grubs.
"We don't believe they have any camping equipment or provisions," a police spokesman told reporters.
"They've already spent two pretty cold nights out there, so we have grave concerns, particularly with children as young as seven months involved," he said.

The air and land search for the group covered an area of up to 7,000 sq km (2,700 square miles) after the woman failed to return with the children on Saturday from a search for bardy grubs, a traditional Aboriginal food, the police spokesman said.
The woman, 27-year-old Aborigine Wanda Schultz, took the children out on Saturday afternoon.

The children, all but one of whom are Aboriginal, are between seven months and 16 years old. Schultz is the mother of five of the children, with the rest belonging to relatives and friends, police said.

Schultz and the children are all from the town of Norseman, 550 km (340 miles) east of Perth in the southwestern pocket of Australia. The group went to nearby Bromus Dam in search of the edible, wood-boring grubs.
All 14 were crammed in a small station wagon which became separated from another car and failed to return as planned on Saturday night.
The woman had led similar expeditions in the area in the past and her car may have broken down or become bogged after recent heavy rain in the area, the spokesman said.
Local Aborigines were helping police with the search, which involved three planes and about 20 four-wheel drive vehicles.
One of the planes was equipped with infra-red sensors capable of picking up body heat.
